advances: Counterexample to raw facet restriction under physical normal-preserving boundary transport, with positive source density and complete actual fibers. No critical-cap stress assumption is used.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The five actual integer fibers have heights $1,2,3,2,1$ times the unit $(d-1)$-box. Their upper own-facets, including the common one at $z=2$, have $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ mass one and normal $e_1$. Use $\mathcal H^0$ on the upper endpoints for $d=1$. All other boundary components have source density one and diagonal transport. On the five upper own-facets give the source densities $(3/4,3/2,1/2,3/2,3/4)$. For each fixed $x'$ the source masses at $0,2,4$ stay in place. The mass at $1$ sends $(1/4,1,1/4)$ to bases $(0,1,2)$, and the mass at $3$ sends the same amounts to bases $(2,3,4)$. The target density at each base is one. The two triples lie on affine upper facets and the symmetric increments give each source its physical mean. The mark and $x'$ are preserved, so this is the claimed actual boundary martingale.

Each upper ambient facet contains three of the upper own-facets. Its source mass is $3/4+3/2+1/2=11/4$ and its target mass is three. The row at base $3$ sends $1/4$ to the common own-facet at base $2$ inside $F_L$, and the row at base $1$ sends $1/4$ there from outside $F_R$. These are the only incoming rows in the displayed coupling. Unequal raw masses rule out any coupling from either raw facet source to its complete target. Both reduced bodies are complete boxes, namely $[0,2]\times[0,1]^{d-1}$ and $[2,4]\times[0,1]^{d-1}$.
statement:
For every $d\ge1$ there is a full-dimensional compact polytope with all its nonempty integer fibers of positive $d$-volume, and a measure $\nu$ with strictly positive density relative to its marked fiber boundary target $\eta$, such that a physical normal-preserving martingale $\nu\to\eta$ exists but the raw restrictions to two nonvertical supporting facets cannot transport to their full unweighted targets. In fact, for
$$
C=\{0\le z\le4,\ -1\le x_1\le\min(z,4-z),\ x'\in[0,1]^{d-1}\}
$$
one can take the two upper facets $F_L=\{x_1=z\}\cap C$ and $F_R=\{x_1=4-z\}\cap C$. Both have continuous normal $e_1$, $\eta(F)=3$, $\nu(F)=11/4$, and incoming mass $1/4$ supported on their common unit-area own-fiber facet at $z=2$.
title: A positive-density boundary martingale leaks into both shared upper facets
